hints: The straightforward loop shifts right once per bit and looks at the lowest one - thirty-one steps whatever the value.
There is a trick that takes one step per bit that is *set*: `value & (value - 1)` clears exactly the lowest one.
Subtracting one turns the lowest set bit into a zero and everything below it into ones; the `and` then wipes all of them out.
So loop while the value is not zero, clearing the lowest set bit each time, and count the rounds.
